Our primary baseline is SfC-NeRF <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">16</a>]</cite>, a density-based method that optimizes volumetric densities through differentiable physics simulation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>]</cite>.
For future prediction, we also compared against GIC <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">3</a>]</cite>, which estimates physical parameters under a fixed dense interior, to test the benefit of explicit interior reconstruction.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Metrics.</span>
For reconstruction, we reported the CD and F-score <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">39</a>]</cite> between the reconstructed and ground-truth particle configurations.
CD measures the geometric proximity, while the F-score evaluates the thresholded reconstruction consistency.
We set the F-score threshold to 0.5% of the maximum bounding-box length and scale CD by <math id="S5.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{3}</annotation></semantics></math> for readability.
For future prediction, we reported the peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index (SSIM) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">44</a>]</cite> for rendered future frames.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Default configuration.</span>
Unless otherwise stated, we followed the default SfC protocol <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">16</a>]</cite>: the cavity size is known, with the Young’s modulus <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E=10^{6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>6</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E=10^{6}</annotation></semantics></math> and Poisson’s ratio <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu=0.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ν</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu=0.3</annotation></semantics></math>.
Each sequence contains <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=14" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>14</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=14</annotation></semantics></math> observed frames rendered from <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M=11" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>11</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M=11</annotation></semantics></math> views around the collision event.
For our method, we used the known-size setting (i) in Section <a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2 Structural Hypothesis Space ‣ 4 Method: Hypothesis-Space Reasoning ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>, initializing the cavity from the observed external geometry without a ground-truth template.
This initialization closely matches centered cavities under size variation, while under position variation, cavities can differ in both position and geometry.
Hyperparameters are fixed across datasets, as described in Section <a href="#S4.SS5" title="4.5 Implementation and Complexity ‣ 4 Method: Hypothesis-Space Reasoning ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.5</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.2 </span>Main Results on the SfC Benchmark</h3>

<div id="S5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We first evaluated hidden-structure reconstruction on the SfC benchmark, which varies the cavity size and position across five external shapes.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Quantitative results.</span>
Table <a href="#S5.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 5.2 Main Results on the SfC Benchmark ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> reports CD and F-score for the size- and position-variation subsets.
Our method outperforms SfC-NeRF in both settings, with larger gains under position variation, where cavity localization is more ambiguous.
This supports the failure analysis in Section <a href="#S3.SS2" title="3.2 Why Density-Based Local Optimization Fails ‣ 3 Problem Setup and Failure Analysis ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a>. Density-based local optimization can be misled when surface-motion discrepancies do not directly indicate the location of hidden cavities.
By evaluating the explicit structural hypotheses through physical simulation, the global stage reduces this ambiguity before Lagrangian particle refinement.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T1" class="ltx_table">

<div id="S5.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">

SfC-NeRF reconstructs a less coherent internal cavity, which can lead to post-collision dynamics that deviate from the observation.
In contrast, our method reconstructs a more coherent cavity structure and better matches the observed sequence.
Additional qualitative results are available in Appendix <a href="#A3" title="Appendix C Qualitative Results ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a> and on the <a href="https://www.kecl.ntt.co.jp/people/kaneko.takuhiro/projects/sfc-hypothesis/" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href">project page</a>.</p>

(b) Effect of geometry-aware losses during Lagrangian particle refinement.
CD values are scaled by <math id="S5.T2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.</figcaption>

<div id="S5.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Framework stages.</span>
Table <a href="#S5.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 5.3 Ablation Study ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>(a) evaluates the framework stages, starting from the exterior-derived cavity instantiation, which encodes a structural prior.
Local refinement improves this initial configuration, while global hypothesis optimization yields a larger improvement by reducing ambiguity in cavity localization.
The full pipeline performs the best, indicating that the structural prior, global ambiguity reduction, and local geometric refinement play complementary roles.
Fig. <a href="#S5.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ 5.2 Main Results on the SfC Benchmark ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>(ii) shows the same trend.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Geometry-aware losses.</span>
Table <a href="#S5.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 5.3 Ablation Study ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>(b) shows that both geometry-aware losses improve the Lagrangian refinement.
The repulsive loss stabilizes the particle spacing, and the volume-preservation loss further improves the reconstruction, with the adaptive variant performing the best.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.4 </span>Interior-Topology Stress Tests</h3>

<div id="S5.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We used the Topology dataset to stress-test reconstruction of more complex and ambiguous interior topologies than those in the standard SfC benchmark.
Table <a href="#S5.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 5.4 Interior-Topology Stress Tests ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> shows how structural assumptions encoded in <math id="S5.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{H}</annotation></semantics></math> affect reconstruction.
The candidate-template setting includes the ground-truth template and assumes a known center, whereas the known-template setting provides both the ground-truth template and center.
These controlled settings are stress tests rather than evidence of arbitrary topology discovery.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T3" class="ltx_table">
<table id="S5.T3.3" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 3: </span>Interior-topology stress tests under different hypothesis-space settings.
We report CD<math id="S5.T3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\downarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\downarrow</annotation></semantics></math> scaled by <math id="S5.T3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{3}</annotation></semantics></math> on symmetric (Sym), asymmetric (Asym), and complex (Comp) subsets.
<em id="S5.T3.15" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Size</em> denotes the known-size setting, <em id="S5.T3.16" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Cand. w/ center</em> uses a set of candidate templates and a known center, and <em id="S5.T3.17" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Template w/ center</em> uses a known template and center.
The upper rows compare methods under the known-size setting, while the lower rows vary structural assumptions.
F-score results are reported in Appendix <a href="#A2.SS2.SSS1" title="B.2.1 F-score Results for Interior-Topology Stress Tests ‣ B.2 Additional Interior-Topology Results ‣ Appendix B Additional Experiments and Analysis ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.2.1</span></a>.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Known-size comparison.</span>
Under the known-size setting, our method outperforms SfC-NeRF across all topology subsets.
The error remains relatively high for Comp, indicating that the detailed reconstruction of complex cavities from collision observations alone is still difficult.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS4.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Effect of structural assumptions.</span>
The lower rows show how changing <math id="S5.SS4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{H}</annotation></semantics></math> affects the result.
A set of candidate templates with a known center enables the global stage to compare structural alternatives before refinement, while a known template and center leave orientation as the main ambiguity.
These rows are not directly comparable because the settings provide different amounts of structural information.
Rather, they show how the same inference framework incorporates different structural assumptions through the hypothesis space.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.5 </span>Future Prediction</h3>

<div id="S5.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A recovered interior structure should support predictive simulation.
We evaluated future prediction on the SfC benchmark under cavity position variation, where incorrect cavity localization strongly affects post-collision dynamics.
Each method used <math id="S5.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=14" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>14</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=14</annotation></semantics></math> observed frames and was evaluated at <math id="S5.SS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+7</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S5.SS5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+14" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>14</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+14</annotation></semantics></math> future frames.
GIC and both variants of our method used the same GIC-based rendering pipeline, including the re-optimization of Gaussian attributes described in Appendix <a href="#A1.SS2.SSS5" title="A.2.5 Re-optimizing Gaussian Attributes ‣ A.2 Model Details ‣ Appendix A Implementation Details ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.2.5</span></a>, while SfC-NeRF used its original PAC-NeRF-based rendering pipeline.
Additional results on the SfC and Topology datasets are provided in Appendix <a href="#A2.SS4" title="B.4 Additional Future Prediction Results ‣ Appendix B Additional Experiments and Analysis ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.4</span></a>.</p>
</div>

</table>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 4: </span>Future prediction on the SfC benchmark under cavity position variation.
PSNR and SSIM are reported at <math id="S5.T4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+7</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S5.T4.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+14" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>14</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+14</annotation></semantics></math> frames beyond the observed window of <math id="S5.T4.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=14" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>14</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=14</annotation></semantics></math> frames.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS5.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Comparison with baselines.</span>
Table <a href="#S5.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 5.5 Future Prediction ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> shows that our full method outperforms GIC and SfC-NeRF at both prediction horizons, particularly at the longer horizon.
The stronger long-horizon performance suggests a benefit from explicit hidden-structure reconstruction for predictive simulation.
We also note that the comparison with SfC-NeRF reflects differences in the rendering pipeline.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS5.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS5.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS5.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Effect of local refinement.</span>
Lagrangian particle refinement corrects residual geometric discrepancies after the global stage and substantially improves prediction at both horizons.
Larger gains in future-frame metrics than in CD may arise because CD measures only the initial reconstructed geometry, while future-frame metrics also reflect the simulated trajectory and can be more sensitive to local geometric differences.
Together with the reconstruction ablation in Section <a href="#S5.SS3" title="5.3 Ablation Study ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.3</span></a>, these results support the complementary roles of the global and local stages.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.6 </span>Robustness and Practical Considerations</h3>

<div id="S5.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluated the robustness of spherical objects from the SfC benchmark under cavity size and position variations, isolating internal-structure ambiguity from external-shape differences.
Table <a href="#S5.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ 5.6 Robustness and Practical Considerations ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> summarizes the representative results for optimizer changes, physical-parameter uncertainty, and degraded observations.</p>
</div>

</table>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 5: </span>Robustness results on spherical objects under cavity size and position variations.
(a) Optimizer variants use the same global objective and simulation budget as the default grid enumeration.
(b) Physical-parameter errors are averaged over positive and negative perturbations; unknown physical parameters are jointly estimated.
(c) Motion blur uses shutter angle <math id="S5.T5.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math>, and half FPS halves the observation frame rate.
CD values are scaled by <math id="S5.T5.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS6.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS6.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS6.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Optimizer sensitivity.</span>
The random search and Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy (CMA-ES) match the default grid enumeration within 0.002 CD, with nearly identical F-scores, suggesting limited sensitivity to the choice of gradient-free optimizer.
Additional ablations are provided in Appendix <a href="#A2.SS1" title="B.1 Global Optimizer and Refinement Ablation ‣ Appendix B Additional Experiments and Analysis ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS6.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS6.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.SS6.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Toward less controlled settings.</span>
Moderate errors in <math id="S5.SS6.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>E</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="S5.SS6.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ν</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu</annotation></semantics></math> and motion blur have little effect.
Joint physical-parameter estimation remains close to the clean setting for size variation but causes moderate degradation for position variation.
Reducing the frame rate also moderately degrades performance in the position subset.
Additional robustness analyses are provided in Appendices <a href="#A2.SS5" title="B.5 Robustness under Relaxed Assumptions ‣ Appendix B Additional Experiments and Analysis ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.5</span></a>–<a href="#A2.SS7" title="B.7 Robustness to Material Variations ‣ Appendix B Additional Experiments and Analysis ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.7</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Limitations and Discussion</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This study has several limitations.
First, our experiments used controlled synthetic data with calibrated cameras and a known simulation model.
Although Section <a href="#S5.SS6" title="5.6 Robustness and Practical Considerations ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.6</span></a> evaluates motion blur and reduced frame rate, real-world capture can introduce additional errors, such as calibration noise and forward-model mismatch. The evaluation on in-the-wild collision sequences remains a topic for future work.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Second, the exact recovery of complex interior topology remains ill-posed.
As shown in Section <a href="#S5.SS4" title="5.4 Interior-Topology Stress Tests ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.4</span></a>, collision observations leave residual ambiguities under weak structural assumptions, particularly for intricate geometries.
Hypothesis-space reasoning makes this trade-off explicit but cannot resolve insufficient observations or structures that are not adequately represented in the hypothesis space.
In the latter case, the global stage can only select the best available mismatched hypothesis, while Lagrangian particle refinement adjusts the geometry but preserves the cavity structure.
Thus, substantial topology changes must be represented in the hypothesis space before refinement.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Future work will include richer structural variables, such as multiple disconnected cavities, anisotropic scaling, and affine transformations, possibly combined with learned shape priors.
CMA-ES performs comparably to coarse-to-fine enumeration in the current low-dimensional settings, while adaptive sampling may become useful as the hypothesis space grows.
Extending the framework to interactions such as squeezing or shaking may also support internal-structure inference from everyday object dynamics.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We presented SfC as hypothesis-space reasoning, replacing implicit density updates with explicit structural hypotheses.
Our two-stage framework combines global hypothesis optimization and Lagrangian particle refinement, separating coarse structural reasoning from fine geometric adjustment.
Experiments showed improved reconstruction and future prediction over the density-based SfC baseline, while topology stress tests and robustness analyses clarified its scope and limitations.
This framework supports the structured inference of the hidden interior structure from collision-induced dynamics.</p>
</div>
</section>

<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Implementation Details</h2>

<section id="A1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.1 </span>Dataset</h3>

<section id="A1.SS1.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">A.1.1 </span>SfC Dataset</h4>

<div id="A1.SS1.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The SfC dataset <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">16</a>]</cite> contains five external shapes: <span id="A1.SS1.SSS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">sphere</span>, <span id="A1.SS1.SSS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">cube</span>, <span id="A1.SS1.SSS1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">bicone</span>, <span id="A1.SS1.SSS1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">cylinder</span>, and <span id="A1.SS1.SSS1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">diamond</span>.
The dataset includes two structural variation subsets used in our main experiments: <span id="A1.SS1.SSS1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">cavity size</span> and <span id="A1.SS1.SSS1.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">cavity position</span>.
In the size variation subset, cavity sizes vary over
<math id="A1.SS1.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{c}\in\left\{0,\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{3},\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{3},\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^{3}\right\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{c}\in\left\{0,\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{3},\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{3},\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^{3}\right\}</annotation></semantics></math>
with the cavity center held fixed.
In the position variation subset, cavity locations vary over
<math id="A1.SS1.SSS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l_{c}\in\{\text{left},\text{right},\text{up},\text{down}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>l</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mtext>left</mtext><mo>,</mo><mtext>right</mtext><mo>,</mo><mtext>up</mtext><mo>,</mo><mtext>down</mtext></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l_{c}\in\{\text{left},\text{right},\text{up},\text{down}\}</annotation></semantics></math>
with the cavity size fixed to <math id="A1.SS1.SSS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{c}=\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{c}=\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.
All objects are composed of elastic material with Young’s modulus <math id="A1.SS1.SSS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E=10^{6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>6</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E=10^{6}</annotation></semantics></math> and Poisson’s ratio <math id="A1.SS1.SSS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu=0.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ν</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu=0.3</annotation></semantics></math>, following the original SfC simulation setting.
In total, the structural benchmark comprises <math id="A1.SS1.SSS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math> external shapes <math id="A1.SS1.SSS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="A1.SS1.SSS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo fence="true" lspace="0em">CLOSE</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(4</annotation></semantics></math> size settings <math id="A1.SS1.SSS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="A1.SS1.SSS1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math> position settings<math id="A1.SS1.SSS1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext=")=40" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" rspace="0em">OPEN</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>40</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">)=40</annotation></semantics></math> sequences.
Representative examples are shown in Fig. <a href="#A1.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ A.1.1 SfC Dataset ‣ A.1 Dataset ‣ Appendix A Implementation Details ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.SSS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Ground-truth dynamics are simulated using the Moving Least Squares Material Point Method (MLS-MPM) simulator <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>]</cite>, in which each object is dropped under gravity and allowed to collide with a ground plane.
Each sequence contains <math id="A1.SS1.SSS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="14" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>14</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">14</annotation></semantics></math> observed frames.
For each deformation state, multiview images are rendered from <math id="A1.SS1.SSS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="11" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>11</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">11</annotation></semantics></math> viewpoints arranged on the upper hemisphere surrounding the object.
Images are rendered with diverse environmental lighting conditions and ground textures to increase visual diversity.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A1.F5" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2611.07900v1/dataset_sfc.png" id="A1.F5.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:679/84;" width="679" height="84" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A1.F5.8" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 5</span>: </span><span id="A1.F5.9" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Overview of the SfC dataset.
For each object, we show a representative observation image and the corresponding ground-truth cross-section.
The dataset contains five external shapes ((a) <span id="A1.F5.9.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">sphere</span>, (b) <span id="A1.F5.9.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">cube</span>, (c) <span id="A1.F5.9.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">bicone</span>, (d) <span id="A1.F5.9.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">cylinder</span>, and (e) <span id="A1.F5.9.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">diamond</span>) with cavity size and position variations.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS1.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">A.1.2 </span>Topology Dataset</h4>

<figure id="A1.F6" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
<figure id="A1.F6.sf1" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><img src="2611.07900v1/dataset_topology_symmetric.png" id="A1.F6.sf1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:679/84;" width="679" height="84" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A1.F6.sf1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">(a)</span> </span><span id="A1.F6.sf1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Symmetric</span></figcaption>
</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
<figure id="A1.F6.sf2" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><img src="2611.07900v1/dataset_topology_asymmetric.png" id="A1.F6.sf2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:679/84;" width="679" height="84" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A1.F6.sf2.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">(b)</span> </span><span id="A1.F6.sf2.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Asymmetric</span></figcaption>
</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
<figure id="A1.F6.sf3" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><img src="2611.07900v1/dataset_topology_complex.png" id="A1.F6.sf3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:679/84;" width="679" height="84" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A1.F6.sf3.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">(c)</span> </span><span id="A1.F6.sf3.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Complex</span></figcaption>
</figure></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A1.F6.18" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 6</span>: </span><span id="A1.F6.19" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Overview of the Topology dataset.
For each shape, we show a representative observation image and the corresponding ground-truth cross-section.
The dataset contains three subsets:
(I) <span id="A1.F6.19.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">symmetric</span> ((a) <span id="A1.F6.19.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">cube</span>, (b) <span id="A1.F6.19.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">cross</span>, (c) <span id="A1.F6.19.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">snowman</span>, (d) <span id="A1.F6.19.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">sun</span>),
(II) <span id="A1.F6.19.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">asymmetric</span> ((e) <span id="A1.F6.19.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">pacman</span>, (f) <span id="A1.F6.19.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">crescent</span>, (g) <span id="A1.F6.19.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">unequal snowman</span>, (h) <span id="A1.F6.19.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">frustum</span>),
and (III) <span id="A1.F6.19.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">complex</span> ((i) <span id="A1.F6.19.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">C-shape</span>, (j) <span id="A1.F6.19.13" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">spherical ring</span>, (k) <span id="A1.F6.19.14" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">split sphere</span>, (l) <span id="A1.F6.19.15" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">triple tunnel</span>).</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We used the Topology dataset to stress-test reconstruction under more complex interior topologies.
Unlike the SfC dataset, which varies cavity size and position, this dataset varies the internal cavity geometry and topology.
It is designed to study how structural assumptions encoded in the hypothesis space affect reconstruction, rather than to evaluate arbitrary topology discovery.
The dataset contains three subsets—<span id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">symmetric</span>, <span id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">asymmetric</span>, and <span id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">complex</span>—each consisting of four cavity shapes.
Representative examples are shown in Fig. <a href="#A1.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ A.1.2 Topology Dataset ‣ A.1 Dataset ‣ Appendix A Implementation Details ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Symmetric set.</span>
The symmetric set contains cavity shapes with discrete rotational symmetry about the object center.
It includes <span id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">cube</span>, <span id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">cross</span>, <span id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">snowman</span>, and <span id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">sun</span>.
The <span id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p2.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">cube</span> defines an axis-aligned rectangular cavity.
The <span id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p2.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">cross</span> is composed of three mutually orthogonal bars.
The <span id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p2.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">snowman</span> consists of two equal spheres arranged along a single axis, exhibiting uniaxial symmetry.
The <span id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p2.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">sun</span> extends conical protrusions in 26 discrete directions from a central sphere.
These shapes provide controlled cases for evaluating the effect of symmetric cavity geometry on reconstruction.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Asymmetric set.</span>
The asymmetric set contains cavity shapes that break symmetry and introduce a preferred orientation.
It includes <span id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">pacman</span>, <span id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">crescent</span>, <span id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p3.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">unequal snowman</span>, and <span id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p3.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">frustum</span>.
The <span id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p3.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">pacman</span> is derived from a sphere by removing an angular wedge, while the <span id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p3.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">crescent</span> is obtained by subtracting a shifted overlapping sphere.
The <span id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p3.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">unequal snowman</span> combines two spheres of different radii to form an elongated asymmetric structure, and the <span id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p3.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">frustum</span> defines a truncated cone with a tapered cross-section.
These shapes test sensitivity to orientation cues in hidden cavity geometry.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Complex set.</span>
The complex set contains cavity shapes with non-trivial topology or spatial discontinuity.
It includes <span id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">C-shape</span>, <span id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p4.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">spherical ring</span>, <span id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p4.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">split sphere</span>, and <span id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p4.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">triple tunnel</span>.
The <span id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p4.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">C-shape</span> forms a partially enclosed shell; the <span id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p4.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">spherical ring</span> retains a cylindrical core within a spherical cavity; and the <span id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p4.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">split sphere</span> produces two disjoint half-spherical cavities displaced along a single axis.
The <span id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p4.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">triple tunnel</span> embeds three orthogonal cylindrical channels within a spherical cavity, yielding a genus-3 topology.
These shapes stress-test reconstruction under high curvature and topological complexity.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">All configurations use a spherical exterior and fixed cavity size <math id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{c}=\left(\tfrac{2}{3}\right)^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{c}=\left(\tfrac{2}{3}\right)^{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.
We generated five random rotations for each shape, yielding <math id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math> shapes <math id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math> subsets <math id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> <math id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math> rotations <math id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="=60" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mn>60</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">=60</annotation></semantics></math> configurations.
Simulation and rendering follow the SfC dataset settings, with <math id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="14" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>14</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">14</annotation></semantics></math> observed frames and <math id="A1.SS1.SSS2.p5.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="11" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>11</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">11</annotation></semantics></math> upper-hemisphere views per sequence.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.2 </span>Model Details</h3>

<div id="A1.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">An overview of the proposed pipeline is shown in Fig. <a href="#S3.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 3.2 Why Density-Based Local Optimization Fails ‣ 3 Problem Setup and Failure Analysis ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> of the main paper.
We describe the implementation details of each step below.</p>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS2.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">A.2.1 </span>Step (0). Dense Initialization</h4>

<div id="A1.SS2.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We initialized the object with a fully dense particle representation using GIC <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">3</a>]</cite>.
GIC first reconstructs a dynamic 3D Gaussian representation from multiview observations and then converts it into a continuum particle representation for MPM simulation.
Each continuum particle is associated with a position, scale, and density value, which are used for simulation and mask rendering.
We used the official GIC implementation and followed its default training configuration.
Below, we describe the GIC-based initialization procedure, including dynamic 3D reconstruction, continuum generation, physical simulation, and velocity estimation.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.SSS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.SSS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Dynamic 3D reconstruction.</span>
GIC reconstructs dynamic scenes using a canonical set of 3D Gaussians and a learned deformation field that maps the canonical configuration to each time step.
The model is trained with L1 and SSIM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">44</a>]</cite> losses, following the architecture and hyperparameters of the official GIC implementation.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.SSS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.SSS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Continuum generation.</span>
From the reconstructed Gaussian representation, we generated a fully dense grid-based point set using a coarse-to-fine strategy.
The initial grid size was set to <math id="A1.SS2.SSS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\mathrm{grid}}^{0}=0.16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>d</mi><mi>grid</mi><mn>0</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mn>0.16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\mathrm{grid}}^{0}=0.16</annotation></semantics></math>, and the grid was upsampled four times.
This yielded a final grid spacing of <math id="A1.SS2.SSS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\mathrm{grid}}=0.16/2^{4}=0.01" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>grid</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>0.16</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0.01</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\mathrm{grid}}=0.16/2^{4}=0.01</annotation></semantics></math>.
This spacing matched the average inter-particle distance used in SfC-NeRF <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">16</a>]</cite>, so that the comparison was not affected by particle density.
In practice, this resolution produced approximately <math id="A1.SS2.SSS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>5</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{5}</annotation></semantics></math> particles for a fully dense object before cavity removal.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.SSS1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.SSS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Physical simulation.</span>
We used a differentiable MPM simulator implemented with DiffTaichi <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>]</cite>.
During simulation, object silhouettes are rendered as alpha masks using 3DGS <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>]</cite>.
These masks are compared with the observed image masks to compute the 2D observation loss.
The simulation parameters, including the material model and time-step settings, follow those used in SfC-NeRF <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">16</a>]</cite> for a fair comparison.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.SSS1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.SSS1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Velocity estimation.</span>
We estimated the pre-collision falling velocity following the procedure used in GIC <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">3</a>]</cite>.
We used four pre-impact frames with the default hyperparameters from the official GIC implementation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">A.2.2 </span>Step (1). Hypothesis Instantiation</h4>

<div id="A1.SS2.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Starting from the dense particle initialization, we instantiated candidate cavity hypotheses using the structural parameterization described in Section <a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2 Structural Hypothesis Space ‣ 4 Method: Hypothesis-Space Reasoning ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a> of the main paper.
Each hypothesis is specified by compact structural variables, including a cavity shape representation, center position, size, and orientation.
The cavity shape representation may be derived from the observed external geometry or selected from a set of templates, depending on the available structural assumptions.
We removed particles inside the resulting cavity region to form the corresponding internal structure.
Structural assumptions fix or restrict a subset of these variables, while the remaining variables are optimized in Step (2).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">A.2.3 </span>Step (2). Global Hypothesis Optimization</h4>

<div id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The global stage evaluates candidate cavity hypotheses using forward-only MPM simulation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">37</a>, <a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>]</cite> and selects the lowest-loss hypothesis.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Default optimizer.</span>
Unless otherwise stated, we used coarse-to-fine enumeration as the default gradient-free optimizer.
This choice is deterministic, reproducible, and consistent with the main experiments.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Position-search regularization.</span>
For position search, we augmented <math id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{global}}(h)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>global</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{global}}(h)</annotation></semantics></math> with the displacement regularizer</p>
<table id="A1.EGx6" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A1.E7"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{disp}}(h)=e^{-k_{\mathrm{disp}}r_{h}}\left\|\widetilde{\bm{\Delta}}_{h}\right\|_{2}^{2}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mi>disp</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>disp</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>h</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo>‖</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝚫</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>h</mi></msub><mo>‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{disp}}(h)=e^{-k_{\mathrm{disp}}r_{h}}\left\|\widetilde{\bm{\Delta}}_{h}\right\|_{2}^{2},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(7)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p3.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{\bm{\Delta}}_{h}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝚫</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>h</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{\bm{\Delta}}_{h}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the cavity displacement from its initial placement in voxel-index units, normalized element-wise by the index span of the object mask along each axis, with each span lower-bounded by one.
The cavity-volume ratio <math id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{h}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{h}</annotation></semantics></math> is the density volume inside the shifted cavity divided by that of the original object.
Hypotheses whose shifted cavity reaches the object boundary are not rendered and are treated as invalid during hypothesis selection.
We minimized <math id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{global}}(h)+w_{\mathrm{disp}}\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{disp}}(h)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>global</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>disp</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mi>disp</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{global}}(h)+w_{\mathrm{disp}}\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{disp}}(h)</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k_{\mathrm{disp}}=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>disp</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k_{\mathrm{disp}}=5</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{\mathrm{disp}}=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>disp</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{\mathrm{disp}}=2</annotation></semantics></math>.
This regularizer discourages cavity displacements that are disproportionately large relative to the object span.
The penalty is measured from the initial cavity placement, with its weight decreasing as the cavity-volume ratio increases.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">For the unknown-size experiment, we instead used <math id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{\mathrm{disp}}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>disp</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{\mathrm{disp}}=1</annotation></semantics></math> and added <math id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{\mathrm{size}}\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{size}}(h)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>size</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mi>size</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{\mathrm{size}}\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{size}}(h)</annotation></semantics></math> to the objective.
The size regularizer is</p>
<table id="A1.EGx7" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A1.E8"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{size}}(h)=\frac{e^{k_{\mathrm{size}}r_{h}}-1}{e^{k_{\mathrm{size}}}-1}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mi>size</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>size</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>h</mi></msub></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>size</mi></msub></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{size}}(h)=\frac{e^{k_{\mathrm{size}}r_{h}}-1}{e^{k_{\mathrm{size}}}-1},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(8)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p4.2" class="ltx_p">with <math id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k_{\mathrm{size}}=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>size</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k_{\mathrm{size}}=5</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{\mathrm{size}}=0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>size</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{\mathrm{size}}=0.1</annotation></semantics></math>.
This regularizer penalizes large cavity-volume ratios and is normalized to <math id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Setting-specific search variables.</span>
The optimized variables and search ranges depend on the hypothesis-space setting, as detailed below.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(i) Known size.</span>
In this setting, we constructed the cavity by offsetting inward from the observed external surface without using a ground-truth template.
The resulting cavity shape and the specified size are fixed, and the default search optimizes only its position.
The default grid optimizer first performs a coarse <math id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5\times 5\times 5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\times 5\times 5</annotation></semantics></math> position search over the three Cartesian axes of the object interior, followed by a refined <math id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5\times 5\times 5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\times 5\times 5</annotation></semantics></math> search around the best candidate.
This evaluates <math id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="250" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>250</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">250</annotation></semantics></math> hypotheses in total (<math id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="125" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>125</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">125</annotation></semantics></math> coarse and <math id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="125" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>125</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">125</annotation></semantics></math> refined), each requiring one forward-only simulation.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(ii) A set of candidate templates and known center.</span>
In this setting, the search considers the four templates used to construct the corresponding topology subset and therefore includes the ground-truth template for each evaluated object.
The coarse stage jointly evaluates the template and orientation by combining all candidate templates with 125 orientations sampled on the sphere using Fibonacci sphere sampling.
The fine stage fixes the template selected in the coarse stage and refines the orientation using 125 cone directions around the selected coarse direction.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p8" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p8.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(iii) Known template and center.</span>
In this setting, we provided the ground-truth template used to construct the evaluated object and its cavity center, leaving orientation as the remaining search variable.
We used the same coarse-to-fine orientation search as in setting (ii): 125 Fibonacci-sphere samples in the coarse stage, followed by 125 cone-direction samples around the selected coarse direction.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p9" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p9.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p9.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Alternative global optimizers.</span>
We also evaluated alternative gradient-free optimizers for the global stage to investigate optimizer sensitivity (Section <a href="#S5.SS6" title="5.6 Robustness and Practical Considerations ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.6</span></a> and Appendix <a href="#A2.SS1" title="B.1 Global Optimizer and Refinement Ablation ‣ Appendix B Additional Experiments and Analysis ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.1</span></a>).
For random search in the position-search setting, the coarse grid enumeration is replaced with uniform random sampling over the same search ranges, while the fine search follows the default grid refinement around the best coarse candidate.
For Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy (CMA-ES) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>]</cite>, the optimizer proposes hypotheses within the same parameter ranges and uses the specified evaluation budget without a separate coarse/fine split.
In the main-paper optimizer-sensitivity evaluation, all optimizer variants are followed by the same Lagrangian particle refinement stage.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p10" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p10.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.SSS3.p10.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Relaxed-assumption settings.</span>
In relaxed-assumption settings (Section <a href="#S5.SS6" title="5.6 Robustness and Practical Considerations ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.6</span></a> and Appendix <a href="#A2.SS5" title="B.5 Robustness under Relaxed Assumptions ‣ Appendix B Additional Experiments and Analysis ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.5</span></a>), we expanded the hypothesis space with additional continuous variables, such as cavity size or physical parameters, to evaluate robustness under relaxed assumptions.
Table <a href="#A1.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ A.2.3 Step (2). Global Hypothesis Optimization ‣ A.2 Model Details ‣ Appendix A Implementation Details ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> summarizes their search ranges and grid resolutions.</p>
</div>

<td id="A1.T6.3.3.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:4.5pt;padding-right:4.5pt;"><span id="A1.T6.3.3.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">5</span></td>
<td id="A1.T6.3.3.4" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:4.5pt;padding-right:4.5pt;"><span id="A1.T6.3.3.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">5</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A1.T6.3.4" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A1.T6.3.4.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:4.5pt;padding-right:4.5pt;"><span id="A1.T6.3.4.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Poisson’s ratio <math id="A1.T6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ν</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu</annotation></semantics></math></span></th>
<td id="A1.T6.3.4.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:4.5pt;padding-right:4.5pt;"><math id="A1.T6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0.1,\,0.4]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">[</mo><mn mathsize="0.900em">0.1</mn><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mn mathsize="0.900em"> 0.4</mn><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0.1,\,0.4]</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 6: </span>Search ranges and grid resolutions for additional continuous variables in relaxed-assumption experiments.
Each parameter is explored using coarse-to-fine grid enumeration with the number of candidates shown for each stage.
The candidate sets exclude the exact ground-truth values to avoid evaluating a trivially correct hypothesis.</figcaption>

</section>
<section id="A1.SS2.SSS4" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">A.2.4 </span>Step (3). Lagrangian Particle Refinement</h4>

<div id="A1.SS2.SSS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">After global hypothesis optimization selected a cavity hypothesis, we refined the corresponding particle configuration following Lagrangian particle optimization <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">15</a>]</cite>.
Starting from <math id="A1.SS2.SSS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathcal{P}}_{h^{\ast}}(t_{1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathcal{P}}_{h^{\ast}}(t_{1})</annotation></semantics></math>, the local stage treats the particles as a Lagrangian system and optimizes their initial positions through differentiable MPM simulation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>]</cite>.
Observation-loss gradients are backpropagated through the full simulated sequence, allowing particle-level refinement under the physical constraints of the simulator.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.SSS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Unless otherwise stated, the objective follows Eq. <a href="#S4.Ex1" title="In 4.4 Lagrangian Particle Refinement ‣ 4 Method: Hypothesis-Space Reasoning ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> in the main paper and combines the 3D surface loss, 2D mask loss, repulsive loss, and volume-preservation loss.
For the repulsive loss, neighboring particle pairs in <math id="A1.SS2.SSS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{rep}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>rep</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{rep}}</annotation></semantics></math> are defined within a radius of <math id="A1.SS2.SSS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.5d_{\mathrm{grid}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.5</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>grid</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.5d_{\mathrm{grid}}</annotation></semantics></math> in the initial configuration.
For the volume-preservation loss, <math id="A1.SS2.SSS4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{V}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{V}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> in <math id="A1.SS2.SSS4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{vol}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>vol</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{vol}}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the material volume estimated by Delaunay tetrahedralization, with <math id="A1.SS2.SSS4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon=10^{-6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon=10^{-6}</annotation></semantics></math>.
We used <math id="A1.SS2.SSS4.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\mathrm{2D}}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\mathrm{2D}}=1</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A1.SS2.SSS4.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\mathrm{rep}}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>rep</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\mathrm{rep}}=1</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A1.SS2.SSS4.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\mathrm{vol}}=10^{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>vol</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\mathrm{vol}}=10^{4}</annotation></semantics></math>.
For the adaptive volume-preservation loss, the reference configuration <math id="A1.SS2.SSS4.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathcal{P}}_{\mathrm{ref}}(t_{1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>ref</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathcal{P}}_{\mathrm{ref}}(t_{1})</annotation></semantics></math> is updated every five iterations.
We performed optimization for <math id="A1.SS2.SSS4.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> iterations using Adam <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">19</a>]</cite>, with learning rate <math id="A1.SS2.SSS4.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.0003125" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.0003125</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.0003125</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="A1.SS2.SSS4.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="=d_{\mathrm{grid}}/32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>grid</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">=d_{\mathrm{grid}}/32</annotation></semantics></math>) and momentum parameters <math id="A1.SS2.SSS4.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta_{1}=0.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta_{1}=0.9</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS2.SSS4.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta_{2}=0.999" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.999</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta_{2}=0.999</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2.SSS5" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">A.2.5 </span>Re-optimizing Gaussian Attributes</h4>

<div id="A1.SS2.SSS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The particle positions obtained by our method define the optimized geometry but do not directly provide the Gaussian appearance attributes required for novel-view rendering.
We therefore ran a fixed-point-cloud 3DGS optimization following the official GIC implementation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">3</a>]</cite>: the particle positions were kept fixed, and only the Gaussian appearance-related attributes were optimized.
This strategy enables novel-view rendering of the optimized and predicted states.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Additional Experiments and Analysis</h2>

<div id="A2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This appendix provides additional experiments and analysis to further characterize the proposed hypothesis-space reasoning framework.
We first analyze global optimizers and Lagrangian particle refinement in more detail (Appendix <a href="#A2.SS1" title="B.1 Global Optimizer and Refinement Ablation ‣ Appendix B Additional Experiments and Analysis ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.1</span></a>).
We then provide supplementary results for the interior-topology stress tests, including F-score results and an additional ablation on the asymmetric subset (Appendix <a href="#A2.SS2" title="B.2 Additional Interior-Topology Results ‣ Appendix B Additional Experiments and Analysis ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.2</span></a>).
We also examine the effect of initialization source to separate the contribution of the optimization framework from that of the initialization representation (Appendix <a href="#A2.SS3" title="B.3 Effect of Initialization Source ‣ Appendix B Additional Experiments and Analysis ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.3</span></a>).
Additional future-prediction results on the SfC and Topology datasets are provided in Appendix <a href="#A2.SS4" title="B.4 Additional Future Prediction Results ‣ Appendix B Additional Experiments and Analysis ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.4</span></a>.
Finally, we evaluate robustness under relaxed structural and physical assumptions (Appendix <a href="#A2.SS5" title="B.5 Robustness under Relaxed Assumptions ‣ Appendix B Additional Experiments and Analysis ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.5</span></a>), analyze sensitivity to physical-parameter errors and material variations (Appendices <a href="#A2.SS6" title="B.6 Robustness to Physical-Parameter Errors ‣ Appendix B Additional Experiments and Analysis ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.6</span></a> and <a href="#A2.SS7" title="B.7 Robustness to Material Variations ‣ Appendix B Additional Experiments and Analysis ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.7</span></a>), and report runtime details (Appendix <a href="#A2.SS8" title="B.8 Runtime Analysis ‣ Appendix B Additional Experiments and Analysis ‣ Structure from Collision via Hypothesis-Space Reasoning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.8</span></a>).</p>
</div>
